parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how a satellite may be in a circular orbit around a planet.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The Earth and the Moon may be considered to be uniform spheres that are isolated in space. The Earth has radius $R$ and mean density $\rho$. The Moon, mass $m$, is in a circular orbit about the Earth with radius $nR$, as illustrated in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1.png}}

The Moon makes one complete orbit of the Earth in time $T$. Show that the mean density $\rho$ of the Earth is given by the expression

$$\rho = \frac{3\pi n^3}{GT^2}.$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The radius $R$ of the Earth is $6.38 \times 10^3\text{km}$ and the distance between the centre of the Earth and the centre of the Moon is $3.84 \times 10^5\text{km}$. The period $T$ of the orbit of the Moon about the Earth is $27.3$ days. Use the expression in (b) to calculate $\rho$.
